concepts.name: Android 16's change to missed scheduleAtFixedRate runs
Long-running workers and their foreground service types
Exposing Compose test tags to UI Automator

questions.prompt: A `ScheduledExecutorService` runs `scheduleAtFixedRate(tick, 0, 1, MINUTES)`. The app's process sits cached for 10 minutes, then comes back. If the app targets API 36 (Android 16), how many missed `tick` runs fire at once?

choices.text: None: missed runs are dropped, and the next tick waits a full minute
All ten, back to back, so the total count of runs still adds up
At most one, and then the schedule carries on at its fixed rate
Ten, but spread over the next minute rather than all at once

questions.explanation: For apps targeting Android 16, `scheduleAtFixedRate()` runs at most one missed execution when the app returns to a valid lifecycle, instead of running every missed one. So code that counts ticks to measure time undercounts after the app was cached. You can test the change with the `STPE_SKIP_MULTIPLE_MISSED_PERIODIC_TASKS` compatibility flag.

sources.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 16 or higher | Android Developers
sources.claim: For apps targeting Android 16, scheduleAtFixedRate() executes at most one missed execution, instead of all missed executions, when the app returns to a valid lifecycle; test with the STPE_SKIP_MULTIPLE_MISSED_PERIODIC_TASKS compat flag.

questions.prompt: A `CoroutineWorker` records GPS for a 30-minute run and calls `setForeground(ForegroundInfo(id, notification))` with no service type. The app targets Android 14. What is missing?

choices.text: Nothing: WorkManager chooses the type from the permissions that the app holds
A call to `startForegroundService()` of your own before the worker even starts
An expedited request, because only expedited work may run over 10 minutes

questions.explanation: WorkManager runs a long-running worker in a foreground service it manages for you. On Android 14+ every long-running worker must specify a foreground service type: pass it in `ForegroundInfo` and declare it on `androidx.work.impl.foreground.SystemForegroundService` in the manifest (`location` here). You don't start a service yourself, and expedited work is a separate feature.

sources.title: Support for long-running workers | Background work | Android Developers
sources.claim: WorkManager runs long-running workers (over 10 minutes) in a foreground service it manages via setForeground(ForegroundInfo); on Android 14+ a foreground service type is required for all long-running workers, passed in ForegroundInfo and declared on SystemForegroundService in the manifest.

questions.prompt: A UI Automator test can't find a `LazyColumn` that has `Modifier.testTag("feed")`, though Compose tests find it fine. Explain why, and how you fix it.

model_answer.summary: UI Automator doesn't see Compose test tags by default; set `testTagsAsResourceId = true` high in the hierarchy and find the node with `By.res("feed")`.
key_points: By default UI Automator finds composables only by descriptors such as displayed text or content description, not by `Modifier.testTag`
Set `Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true }` high in the hierarchy (on the `Scaffold`, say) so nested test tags are exposed as resource IDs
Then find it with `By.res("feed")`, not `By.res(package, id)`, which is formatted differently from the test tag

questions.explanation: Compose test tags live in the semantics tree that Compose tests read; UI Automator reads the accessibility view of the screen, so the tags must be mapped to resource IDs first.

sources.title: Interoperability | Jetpack Compose | Android Developers
sources.claim: Composables are accessible from UiAutomator only by descriptors like text or content description unless testTagsAsResourceId is enabled high in the hierarchy; then a Modifier.testTag can be found with By.res(resourceName), not By.res(resourcePackage, resourceId).

questions.prompt: Your app counts `scheduleAtFixedRate` ticks to track how long a workout session has run. Explain what Android 16 changes for this code, and how you would fix and test it.

model_answer.summary: Targeting Android 16, missed fixed-rate runs collapse to at most one when the app returns, so tick counts undercount; measure elapsed time from timestamps and test with the compat flag.
key_points: For apps targeting Android 16 (API 36), `scheduleAtFixedRate()` runs at most one missed execution when the app returns to a valid lifecycle, instead of all of them
So counting ticks undercounts time spent while the app was cached; compute elapsed time from stored timestamps instead
Test the new behaviour with the compatibility framework's `STPE_SKIP_MULTIPLE_MISSED_PERIODIC_TASKS` flag

questions.explanation: Before Android 16, all missed runs fired at once on return, which hid the design flaw of using a tick count as a clock. The fix is to stop relying on the executor's catch-up.

sources.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 16 or higher | Android Developers
sources.claim: For apps targeting Android 16, scheduleAtFixedRate() executes at most one missed execution, instead of all missed executions, when the app returns to a valid lifecycle; test with the STPE_SKIP_MULTIPLE_MISSED_PERIODIC_TASKS compat flag.

questions.prompt: How does WorkManager run a worker that calls `setForeground()`?

choices.text: It moves the worker to a new process that the system won't kill for memory
It turns the request into an exact alarm, so Doze can't hold it back
It runs it in a foreground service it manages, with your notification
It schedules a UIDT job instead, which standby quotas don't apply to

questions.explanation: For long-running work, WorkManager manages and runs a foreground service on your behalf to execute the request, showing the notification from your `ForegroundInfo`. This is what lets a worker run longer than 10 minutes; it is not an alarm, a separate process or a UIDT job.

sources.title: Support for long-running workers | Background work | Android Developers
sources.claim: Under the hood, WorkManager manages and runs a foreground service on your behalf to execute the WorkRequest, while also showing a configurable notification; this supports workers that run longer than 10 minutes.

questions.prompt: You set `Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true }` on your `Scaffold`. Which UI Automator selector finds a child with `Modifier.testTag("feed")`?

choices.text: `By.text("feed")`, since test tags become the node text
`By.res("feed")`, with the test tag as resource name

questions.explanation: With `testTagsAsResourceId` enabled, a test tag is exposed as a resource name, so `By.res("feed")` finds it. The two-argument `By.res(package, id)` builds a differently formatted name and won't match. Test tags don't become text or content descriptions.

sources.title: Interoperability | Jetpack Compose | Android Developers
sources.claim: Any composable with Modifier.testTag(tag) can be accessed with By.res(resourceName) using the tag as resourceName; use By.res(resourceName) only, not By.res(resourcePackage, resourceId), which formats differently.
